name: Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow')
principle: The code copies an input buffer into an output buffer without proving the input length is less than the destination capacity. If the source is longer, the copy writes past the destination and can corrupt memory, crash, or redirect control flow.
detection_signals: strcpy(dst, src) where dst is char[N] or fixed heap buffer and src is externally influenced
strcat(dst, src) where remaining capacity of dst is not checked before append
sprintf(dst, ...) writing into fixed-size char buffer instead of snprintf(dst, sizeof dst, ...)
gets(dst) reading into any fixed-size buffer
scanf("%s", dst) or fscanf(...,"%s", dst) without a field width
memcpy(dst, src, len) or strncpy(dst, src, len) where len derives from input and is not bounded by sizeof(dst)
for/while loop copying src[i] to dst[i] without i < dst_capacity guard
negative_signals: snprintf(dst, sizeof(dst), "%s", src) or equivalent capacity-bounded formatting
copy is preceded by if (strlen(src) < sizeof(dst)) or equivalent destination-capacity check
scanf format uses a width matching the buffer, e.g. scanf("%19s", buf) for char buf[20]
strncpy/memcpy length argument is min(sizeof(dst)-1, source_length) and dst is explicitly NUL-terminated
destination is dynamically allocated from checked source length, e.g. malloc(strlen(src)+1) with overflow check
false_defense_traps: Replacing strcpy with strncpy without forcing dst[sizeof(dst)-1]='\0'
Using sizeof(ptr) instead of the real allocation size for a heap buffer
Relying only on ASLR, DEP/NX, stack canaries, /GS, or FORTIFY_SOURCE
Client-side length validation without server-side validation
Denylisting bad characters while allowing overlong input
verification_focus: Does every buffer copy prove the maximum bytes written, including the terminator, fit within the destination capacity?

consequence_chains.trigger: source length exceeds destination capacity during copy
overflow overwrites a pointer, length, or destination address used by a later write
consequence_chains.consequence: write-what-where primitive and possible control-flow hijack

consequence_chains.trigger: length check allows exactly destination size but code also writes a NUL terminator

patch_principle: Replace unbounded copy APIs with capacity-bounded APIs and pass the real destination size.
Validate or truncate input length before copying, including space for the NUL terminator.
Allocate destination buffers from checked source length instead of fixed guesses.
Add compiler/runtime hardening as defense in depth, not as the primary fix.
